newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish central bank seen wanting lower 1-day rates.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank seen wanting lower 1-day rates.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland (NBP) on Tuesday rejected all 266 million zlotys worth of bids at today's reverse-repo operation, which the money market took as a sign that the central bank wants to see lower one-day rates.
"It seems the central bank signalled that (one-day) cash doesn't need to be so expensive," said Radoslaw Radziszewski, deputy chief dealer of Pekao SA.
On Tuesday, one-day rates were quoted between 19.90 and 21.50 percent versus the last 14-day reverse repo maximum accepted rate of 19.13 percent on September 25. @

Dealers said one-day rates were high because banks were reluctant to create even small gaps in October's required reserve after many were caught short last month and one-day rates suged above 25 percent on September's last trading day.
There was no immediate movement in one-day rates after the results of the reverse repo operation were announced.
